chunks: As for the hadith of Ṣafwān ibn Mihrān al-Jammāl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
And I asked him about the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, so he said: “If you have omitted something, then before the taslīm; and if you have added something, then after it.”

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the concluding salutation ending the prayer
key_terms.زِدْتَ: you added something to the prayer
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed to remedy forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.فَبَعْدَهُ: then after it, meaning after the taslim
key_terms.نَقَصْتَ: you omitted or reduced something from the prayer

ai.seo_question: When are the two sajdahs of forgetfulness performed before or after the taslim in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sajdat al-sahw in salat (prayer). It distinguishes between omission and addition in the prayer: for omission, the two prostrations are before the taslim, and for addition, they are after it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.995 - As for the narration of Safwan ibn Mehran al-Jammal from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"I asked him about the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdat al-Sahw),
Imam (as) said: 'If you have made a mistake by reducing something in your prayer, then [perform the prostrations] before the Tasleem. But if you have added something, then [perform the prostrations] after the Tasleem.'"
